_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Fourth municipal-level slice in the AF branch (G.13). Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review.
_note: This is the strongest positive municipal-level finding of the batch, and by a wide margin. South Africa's municipal budgeting system explicitly and repeatedly ties itself to StatsSA's CPI: the City of Johannesburg's own 2026/27-2028/29 MTREF budget book states it is 'projecting CPI at 3.4 per cent for the 2026/27 financial year... CPI averaged 3.2 per cent in 2025 (StatsSA)', ties minor-service tariff increases and property-rates revenue growth directly to that projected figure, and pegs collective-bargained wage increases to 'the average CPI for the period... The source of CPI data is StatsSA' (with a 4-7% collar). This traces to a real institutional chain, not a coincidence: National Treasury's own annual MFMA budget circulars (independently located and opened, not just cited secondhand) mandate the CPI benchmark and the wording Johannesburg's budget book uses ('required to justify all increases more than CPI') is close to verbatim from Circular 129/132's own language. The one genuine gap: the City's own Property Rates Policy document, searched in full, contains no CPI clause at all -- the annual percentage increase is set separately each year in the budget book/Council resolution, not in the Policy. City Power's own site could not be reached (persistent SSL/robots errors) so its tariff document's CPI basis, if any, is unverified rather than denied.

A candidate Integrated Development Plan document ('The People's Plan 2025/26') was located via search but not fetched/verified, since the MTREF budget book already contained an explicit IDP-alignment section and was the higher-priority source. Worth opening directly in a future session as its own node.

reports.title: City of Johannesburg Medium-Term Budget 2026/27 – 2028/29
reports.description: The City of Johannesburg's own MTREF budget book, covering operating and capital budgets, tariff setting, and budget assumptions. States the City is "projecting CPI at 3.4 per cent for the 2026/27 financial year" (sourced from StatsSA) and that "municipalities are required to justify in their budget documentation all increases more than CPI." Ties wage increases directly to StatsSA CPI (with a 4-7% collar) and property-rates/minor-service tariff growth to the same projected figure.
reports.cadence_note: Annual MTREF budget cycle (tabled and final versions each May, covering a rolling three-year medium-term period); this entry refers to the final approved 2026/27–2028/29 budget book.

reports.title: City of Johannesburg Property Rates Policy 2025/26
reports.description: The City's own rates policy adopted under the Local Government: Municipal Property Rates Act, No. 6 of 2004, governing property categories, differential rates, exemptions and rebates. Full-text search found no CPI/inflation-indexation clause in this document itself; the annual percentage increase is set separately each year via Council budget resolution, not in the Rates Policy.
reports.cadence_note: Reviewed and re-adopted annually alongside the MTREF budget cycle.

reports.title: Local Government: Municipal Finance Management Act, No. 56 of 2003
reports.publisher: Parliament of South Africa / National Treasury
reports.description: National framework law governing municipal budgeting for all South African municipalities, including Johannesburg. Section 20(1)(b)(iii) empowers the Minister of Finance to prescribe "inflation projections to be used with regard to the budget"; Section 42(3)(b)(i) requires bulk resource (electricity/water) price-increase submissions to explain how they take account of "the national government's inflation targets."

reports.title: National Treasury MFMA Municipal Budget Circulars (e.g. Circular No. 129, Circular No. 132) for the MTREF
reports.description: National Treasury's annual guidance circulars to all municipalities on preparing MTREF budgets, including mandated macroeconomic CPI forecast tables and the requirement that "municipalities are required to justify all increases more than the projected inflation target" in their budget narratives, plus the Cost Reflective Tariff Tool referenced by name in Circular 132.
reports.cadence_note: Issued in pairs (e.g. 129/130, 132/134) around December and March/June each MTREF cycle.

reports.title: Local Government: Municipal Property Rates Act, No. 6 of 2004
reports.description: The national enabling law under which the City of Johannesburg's Property Rates Policy is adopted. Section 17(3) allows the Minister, with the Minister of Finance, to "increase the monetary threshold referred to in subsection (1)(h) to reflect inflation" -- the only inflation-linked provision found in the Act's text; there is no general CPI-linked cap on annual rates increases in the Act itself.

dependencies.basis: "CPI averaged 3.2 per cent in 2025 (StatsSA)... The City is projecting CPI at 3.4 per cent for the 2026/27 financial year" and, for wage/salary increases, "The source of CPI data is StatsSA."

"It should be noted that the budget is in line with the national budget (Division of Revenue Bill) as presented by the Minister of Finance..." and "The cost of the social package of the registered indigent households is largely financed by national government through the local government equitable share received in terms of the annual Division of Revenue Act."

"NT has developed a Cost Reflective Tariff Tool (MFMA Circular 132) which municipalities should complete... Municipalities are required to justify in their budget documentation all increases more than CPI." This mirrors near-verbatim the National Treasury circular's own language: "municipalities are required to justify all increases more than the projected inflation target."

The circular's macroeconomic table sources CPI Inflation forecasts to 'National Treasury Budget Review 2025,' and the companion circular states 'The Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation is forecasted to be 4.4 per cent' as the benchmark municipalities must justify against. Flagged as an indirect (Budget Review-mediated) rather than direct-quoted StatsSA link within the circular text itself.

MFMA s.20(1)(b)(iii) empowers the Minister to prescribe 'inflation projections to be used with regard to the budget,' and s.42(3)(b)(i) requires bulk-resource price submissions to address 'the national government's inflation targets' -- a framework-level statutory hook, though the Act's own text does not name StatsSA or CPI by acronym.

Rates Policy: adopted under 'Local Government: Municipal Property Rates Act, No. 6 of 2004 ("the MPRA")'; the City's MTREF budget book separately states 'Property Rates are levied in terms of the Local Government: Municipal Property Rates Act, 6 of 2004 (the Act) as amended, read with the Council's Rates Policy.'

_dropped.edge: Johannesburg Water tariff schedule / council motivation report CPI basis
_dropped.why: Both Johannesburg Water's 'Combined tariffs 2026-2027' schedule and its Council motivation report ('ITEM 77 -- Amendment of Tariff Charges for Water Services and Sewerage and Sanitation Services: 2026/27') were fully text-searched and contain zero occurrences of CPI/inflation. Their stated rationale is water scarcity and Municipal Systems Act cost-reflectivity principles, not CPI -- a documented absence, not a missed search.

The budget book states only that the City's Expanded Social Package Policy 'will be reviewed to ensure that it is aligned to national government policies supporting indigent customers' -- a vague, unnamed reference that does not name the National Framework for Municipal Indigent Policies specifically.

_dropped.why: Full-text search of the consolidated Municipal Property Rates Act 6 of 2004 found only one inflation-related clause (s.17(3)), concerning a Gazette-notice monetary exemption threshold -- not a general cap on annual rates percentage increases.
